title: Where Your Tax Refund Should Go (A Simple Decision Path)

lines.say: Getting a tax refund this year?
Decide where it goes now, before it lands and quietly disappears.

lines.cap: Our example: a $2,000 refund, arriving in March.
lines.say: Our example: a two thousand dollar refund, arriving in March.
Here's a simple decision path, one question at a time.

lines.cap: First, take 10% for something fun: $200. You'll stick to a plan better when part of it is yours.
lines.say: First, take ten percent for something fun. Two hundred dollars. You'll stick to a plan better when part of it is yours.
Then ask four questions, in order. Stop at the first no.

scene.head: ASK IN ORDER · STOP AT THE FIRST NO
scene.foot: All yes? It goes to your bigger savings goals.

lines.say: Here they are.
One. Are all your bills caught up? If not, the refund catches them up. Late fees and shutoffs cost more than anything.
Two. Do you have a starter emergency fund, one month of bills? If not, start there.
Three. Is your high-interest debt gone? If not, that's where it goes.
Four. Are your sinking funds on track? If not, top them up.
All yes? Then it goes to your bigger savings goals.
Here's why question three beats a savings account.

lines.cap: $1,800 in savings at 4% earns about $72 in a year. Put on a 24% card, it saves about $432 in interest.
lines.say: Eighteen hundred in savings at four percent earns about seventy-two dollars in a year. Put it on a twenty-four percent card, and it saves about four thirty-two in interest.

lines.cap: On the $10,000 card from episode 11, paying $500 a month, that $1,800 finishes it 5 months sooner and saves about $905 in interest.
lines.say: On the ten thousand dollar card from episode eleven, paying five hundred a month, that eighteen hundred finishes it five months sooner, and saves about nine hundred in interest.
One more thing.

scene.text: A big refund means you overpaid all year.

lines.say: A big refund means you overpaid tax all year. In the US, you can adjust your W-4 withholding, so that money comes in each paycheck instead.

scene.label: A $2,000 refund, spread over 26 paychecks
scene.sub: more in every paycheck, if you adjust withholding

lines.cap: $2,000 spread over 26 paychecks is about $77 more per check.
lines.say: Two thousand, spread over twenty-six paychecks, is about seventy-seven dollars more per check.
Some people like the forced savings of a refund, and that's fine. Just make it a choice. If you're unsure, ask a tax professional.
